videos.caption: The one prompt edit with Claude, step by step. No DM for resources, it's all right here. 1. Install Claude Code (Codex works too). Download the desktop app. 2. Open Claude Code. It opens in Chat, so switch it over to Code. 3. Make a folder on your computer. Mine is called My Boss Editor. 4. Select the folder: Local, then Open folder. That's your workspace. 5. Copy these GitHub repositories: • FFmpeg: every cut, crop, mix, mute and render · github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg • faster-whisper: word-level transcription every cut is placed against · github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper • Whisper: OpenAI's speech model that faster-whisper runs · github.com/openai/whisper • yt-dlp: downloads the source video · github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp • OpenCV + contrib: follows whoever is talking in the vertical crop · github.com/opencv/opencv and github.com/opencv/opencv_contrib • Puppeteer: headless Chrome that renders the captions and titles to video · github.com/puppeteer/puppeteer • HyperFrames: agent-built motion graphics from HTML · github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes 6. Prompt Claude and give it the links: "You are my short form editor. Here are all the GitHub links to help you do your job." 7. Find an edit you like and send it: "I like the style of this reel. Can we duplicate this style and use it for a video of mine?" 8. Shoot your video. 9. Send it to Claude. Copy the path of the file and paste it in. 10. Review it and use your voice to edit. Bonus: turn it into a skill. "Hey, turn this into a skill." Next time it knows the process. This was not me going into a timeline. Claude edited it in the same list style as the reel I sent it. His problem with it: tell a model to act like a good accountant and it starts playing one. You get the vocabulary. You don't get the method. The research says the same. One study ran 162 roles across 2,410 factual questions on four model families and found personas didn't beat using no persona at all. Picking the "best" role per question worked about as well as picking at random. Wharton's Generative AI Labs repeated it with six models on graduate-level science, engineering and law questions, 25 runs each. Expert personas made no real difference, and mismatched ones sometimes made things worse. Personas moved tone, not accuracy. So he asks for the thing underneath instead. The techniques, the tools, the knowledge a professional would actually use. Then the part people get backwards. He wants it explained to him like he's 5. The 4 levels of using AI at work How to use AI at work: there are four levels, and most people never leave level one. Chat. You paste something into ChatGPT or Claude, it answers, you copy it back out. Useful, but you're the delivery guy carrying every answer between your apps by hand. Context. Give it your price list, your process docs and ten emails you wrote so it learns how you sound. Same AI, completely different answers, because now it answers like it works at your company. Connected tools. Out of the box, AI can't open your CRM or read your spreadsheet. Almost every app has a door for other software called an API, and MCP is a standard plug that lets AI walk through those doors. Once it's connected, it sees your contacts, your sheets and your email, and it acts: update, send, create. Updating 2,000 customer records from last month's invoices is two weeks of somebody's life. Connected AI does it in minutes. Run it on ten records first, check them, then let it do the rest. Automations. Level three still needs you to ask. Level four starts on its own: a new lead comes in, an invoice lands, Monday at 8am. A tool like n8n moves the data between your apps, and the AI in the middle does the thinking: reads the email, picks the category, writes the reply. Your business keeps running while you sleep. The whole ladder: chat, context, connected tools, automations. On level three you talk and it does the work. On level four you don't even have to talk. If you want to climb all four, from your first chat to your first AI automation, I built seven courses for exactly that, in order, inside my community.
